brief: Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted: macro has turned harder and AI/large-cap tech positioning is no longer a clear tailwind, so clients have re-engaged tech on macro uncertainty, pushing prime-book net Mag7 exposure to near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since the start of 2022, even as overall net exposure stays low with some cheap, under-owned pockets. US Power (GSENEPOW) positioning is extremely clean (15th percentile, 3-year lookback) and the desk treats the midterms as a clearing event, recommending the Power Up America basket on low positioning, normalized valuation and intact fundamentals; IPP sentiment is turning less negative. Dated catalysts: the FERC ruling on PJM's large-load framework (October 12), PJM RBP filings, and the ERCOT data-center interconnection audit. The desk expects earnings revisions higher as IPPs sign mega-cap PPAs (CEG's 700MW PJM nuclear deal, CEG-Google's 3.6GW nuclear PPA) and flags Palladium Calls given fragmented, state-level power markets. Separately, GIR raises data-center capacity forecasts to about 250GW by 2030 (ANET/CLS/HPE/CSCO positioned on networking), values European utilities' grid connection points at about €20bn (Solaria monetizing its access could add about 45% to its share price), and lifts its 2030 behind-the-meter power forecast from 40GW to 67GW.
